6.1.rationale: The cited provisions establish general protection for women and children from violence and discrimination and provide services such as safe houses for women/child victims of violence, but they do not identify women or girls in conflict, disaster, emergency, or displacement/refugee situations as a specific target group. The only explicit emergency-situation reference is limited to children (special protection for children in emergency situations), which is insufficient under the coding rules.

6.2.rationale: The policy explicitly mentions trafficking in persons within its objectives and definitions (including trafficking in persons as part of the protection mandate and P2TP2A scope) and also cites the national anti-trafficking law in its legal basis, which is sufficient to include trafficking victims within scope.

6.3.rationale: The cited text involves encouraging the business sector to socialize women/children’s rights and dangers of violence to employees, but it does not identify women workers/female employees as a specific vulnerable target group nor provide workplace-specific protection measures for women workers against violence/exploitation. References are general to women and children rather than women workers specifically.

6.4.rationale: None of the cited sentences mention elderly women or provide any special protection measures targeted to elderly women.

6.5.rationale: The only disability-related reference in the cited text is a prohibition on discriminatory treatment of women and children with disabilities, plus a child-only category of “children with disabilities” under special protection. Under the coding rules, non-discrimination alone and child-only disability provisions are insufficient to count as special protection for women with disabilities or people with disabilities generally.

6.6.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention women heads of household/families or provide any special protection measures targeted to them.

6.7.rationale: The only minority/isolated reference is for children (“children from minority and isolated groups”) within child special protection. There is no explicit mention of women from minority/isolated groups as beneficiaries of protection measures, so the criterion is not met.

Every woman and child who becomes a witness or perpetrator of violence has the right to receive information, protection, rehabilitation, confidential handling, psychological and legal assistance, as well as fulfillment of their rights related to their status as a wife, mother, child, family member or as a community member.
6.8.rationale: The policy explicitly includes women who are witnesses or perpetrators of violence as entitled to protection and services, which covers women involved in legal processes as witnesses and perpetrators (i.e., women in conflict with the law in these roles).

6.9.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention Indigenous peoples, customary communities (masyarakat adat), or equivalent Indigenous groups as beneficiaries of special protection or services.

6.10.rationale: The cited text does not mention refugees, displacement, or forced displacement. References to safe houses and repatriation/social reintegration are framed for victims of violence generally and do not explicitly target refugees or displaced persons.

6.11.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention domestic workers as a target group or provide any special protection measures specifically for domestic workers.

6.12.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention homelessness or women experiencing homelessness. Safe house provisions are tied to women/child victims of violence needing continuous handling, not homelessness as such.

6.13.rationale: The cited sentences do not mention former inmates or formerly incarcerated women as a target group, nor do they provide special protection measures for them. Cooperation with correctional community supervisors is not framed as protection for former inmates.
